hypothesis_or_reduction_question: Does residual-loser-specific recovery retain an advantage over a generic symmetric recurrent-memory reduction when both receive the same two-scalar state budget and one independently DEV-selected decay parameter?
implementation_or_experiment_performed: Implemented two matched two-state/one-decay mechanisms; independently selected decay on fixed DEV utility and evaluated the selected decay on disjoint TEST seeds across seven fixed false-revision/return-latency utility trade-offs.
observations: Symmetric recurrent TEST utility exceeded residual-loser TEST utility for all seven fixed trade-offs, with gaps from +0.006151 to +0.030186.
what_would_falsify_or_reduce_it: A fresh matched prospective H2 design in which loser-specific retention retains a preregistered held-out advantage over strong recurrent/probabilistic memory controls under matched information, state, training/tuning and resource budgets.
candidate_formal_question: Under matched state, information, training/tuning and resource budgets, does loser-specific residual retention improve a preregistered recovery-vs-false-revision utility beyond generic recurrent/probabilistic memory?
promotion_recommendation_scope: Reject this current toy as a formalization candidate only; retain the reduction lesson. This is not a formal rejection of H2.
